Figure: Grid search result heatmap for spike threshold


data <- read.csv("data_heatmap.csv", T)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(Threshold = as.factor(Threshold), 
         Problem = factor(Problem, levels = unique(data$Problem)[4:1]))

heatmap_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Threshold, y = Problem, fill = Accuracy)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Accuracy, 4)), color = "black", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = 1) +
  labs(
    title = expression(paste("Grid search result heatmap for spike threshold (", theta, ")")),
    x = expression(paste("Spike Threshold (", theta, ")")),
    y = "Problem Category",
    fill = "Accuracy"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) + # 기본 텍스트 크기 조절
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16), # 제목 중앙 정렬 및 굵게
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )


data <- data %>%
  mutate(Threshold = as.factor(Threshold), 
         Problem = factor(Problem, levels = unique(data$Problem)[4:1])) %>%
  group_by(Problem) %>%
  mutate(
    Normalized_Accuracy = (Accuracy - min(Accuracy)) / (max(Accuracy) - min(Accuracy)),
    Normalized_Accuracy = if_else(is.nan(Normalized_Accuracy), 0.5, Normalized_Accuracy)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


heatmap_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Threshold, y = Problem, fill = Normalized_Accuracy)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Accuracy, 4)), color = "black", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", direction = 1, begin = 0.3, end = 0.95) +
  labs(
    title = expression(paste("Grid search result heatmap for spike threshold (", theta, ")")),
    x = expression(paste("Spike Threshold (", theta, ")")),
    y ='', #"Problem",
    fill = "Normalized\nAccuracy" # [수정] 범례 제목 변경
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + # 기본 텍스트 크기 조절
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16), # 제목 중앙 정렬 및 굵게
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, color = 'black'),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = 'black'),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

# 4. 플롯 출력
print(heatmap_plot)

Figure: Performance evaluation based on data features



dat = read.table("result_table1.txt", sep = "-")

# Data preprocessing for input of plot function
{
  dat = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", dat$V1)
  dat = round(as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(dat, split= ','))),3)
  
  df = data.frame(score = dat)
  
  # Feature Definition
  df$metric = c('Accuracy', 'Recall', 'Precision', 'F1')
  df$window = c(rep(5,16),rep(10,16),rep(15,16),rep(20,16))
  df$indicator = c(rep('single', 64), rep('interactive', 64), rep('integrated', 64))
  
  df$problem = c(rep('Intimacy and non-Intimacy', 4),
                 rep('Empathy and non-Empathy', 4),
                 rep('Competition and Cooperation', 4),
                 rep('Low focus and High focus', 4))
  
  df$indicator = factor(df$indicator, levels = c('single','interactive', 'integrated') )
  df$problem = factor(df$problem, levels = c('Intimacy and non-Intimacy',
                                             'Empathy and non-Empathy',
                                             'Competition and Cooperation', 
                                             'Low focus and High focus') )
  
  # Reorder feature columns
  df = df[,c(2:5,1)]
  df2 = dcast(df,  window + indicator + problem ~ metric)
  df2 = df2[, c(3,2,1,4,6,7,5)]
  df2 = df2[order(df2$problem, df2$indicator, df2$window),]
  
  # Save summarized data
  write.csv(df2, "result_table1.csv", row.names = F)
  df$window = factor(df$window)
  df = df[which(df$metric == 'Accuracy'),]
}

# (Visualization 1) Bar plot
mycol = brewer.pal(n = 9, "PuBu")[6:9] # Colors
names(df)[3] = 'indicator:'



ggplot(df,                                      # Grouped barplot using ggplot2
       aes(x = as.numeric(as.character(window)),
           y = score,
           colour = `indicator:`,
           label =score
       )) +
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point(aes(shape=`indicator:`), size =2)+
  xlab("Window size") + 
  ylab("Accuracy") +
  ylim(c(0.5, 1) ) +
  # geom_text_repel(vjust = -1.1, size = 2.9, fontface = "bold",show.legend = F) +
  # scale_color_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#FC4E07", "#00AFBB")) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette="Set1") + 
  facet_wrap(~problem, nrow =2 ,scales="free") +
  theme_test(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", 
        legend.title = element_text(size=10, color = 'black'), 
        legend.text = element_text(size=10, color = 'black'),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.7, 'cm'))

Figure: Performance evaluation based on data encoding methods


dat = read.table("result_table2.txt", sep = "-")

# Data preprocessing for input of plot function
{
  dat = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", dat$V1)
  dat = round(as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(dat, split= ','))),3)
  
  df = data.frame(score = dat)
  df$metric = c('Accuracy', 'Recall', 'Precision', 'F1')
  df$indicator = c(rep('single', 16), rep('interactive', 16), rep('integrated', 16))
  df$spike_encoding = c(rep('Solid', 48), rep('Dot', 48), rep('Raw', 48))
  df$loss = c(rep('L_M', 144), rep('L_S', 144))
  df$problem = c(rep('Intimacy and non-Intimacy', 4),rep('Empathy and non-Empathy', 4),rep('Competition and Cooperation', 4),rep('Low focus and High focus', 4))
  df$indicator = factor(df$indicator, levels = c('single','interactive', 'integrated') )
  df$problem = factor(df$problem, levels = c('Intimacy and non-Intimacy',
                                             'Empathy and non-Empathy',
                                             'Competition and Cooperation', 
                                             'Low focus and High focus') )
  df$spike_encoding = factor(df$spike_encoding, levels = c('Raw','Dot', 'Solid') )
  df$loss = factor(df$loss)
  
  df2 = df[which( (df$metric == 'Accuracy') & (df$loss =='L_S')  ),]
}


# (Visualization 1) Bar plot
names(df2)[4] = 'spike encodings:'
ggplot(df2, aes(x = indicator, y = score, fill = `spike encodings:`, label = score)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", alpha = 0.6, colour = "gray25")  +
  labs(x="Indicator", y="Accuracy") +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  geom_text(position = position_dodge(width = 1), 
            vjust = -0.3, size = 2.9, colour = 'grey20') +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.39,1),oob = scales::squish)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#FC4E07", "#00AFBB")) +
  facet_wrap(~problem,nrow =2 ,scales="free") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", 
        legend.title = element_text(size=10),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.7, 'cm'))

plot_data_integrated$problem_short <- factor(plot_data_integrated$problem_short,

position_dodge_val <- 0.8

Figure: Performance evaluation based on loss functions


filtered_data <- df %>%
  filter(metric == 'Accuracy', 
         spike_encoding == 'Solid')

names(filtered_data)[5] = 'loss function:' # Applying the index rename as requested
filtered_data$score = round(as.numeric(filtered_data$score), 3)


# 2. Summarize Data: Average across the 4 problems and calculate SD
plot_data_avg <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(indicator, `loss function:`) %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean_Accuracy = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Accuracy = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# 3. Create the Averaged Bar Plot with Error Bars
position_dodge_val <- 0.8
ggplot(plot_data_avg, 
       aes(x = indicator, 
           y = Mean_Accuracy, 
           fill = `loss function:`, # Fill by the renamed loss function column
           group = `loss function:`,
           label = round(Mean_Accuracy, 3))) +
  
  # Bar Plot
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = position_dodge_val), 
           width = 0.7) + 
  
  # Standard Deviation Error Bars
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean_Accuracy - SD_Accuracy, 
                    ymax = Mean_Accuracy + SD_Accuracy), 
                position = position_dodge(width = position_dodge_val),
                width = 0.2, 
                alpha = 0.9) +
  
  # Value Labels
  geom_text(aes(y = Mean_Accuracy + SD_Accuracy), # Position label at top of error bar
            position = position_dodge(width = position_dodge_val),
            vjust = -0.5, # Slightly above the error bar
            size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  # Styling
  labs(x="Indicator", 
       y="Average Accuracy (+/- SD)",
       title = "Average Accuracy by Indicator and Loss Function") +
  
  # Use original Y-axis limits and squish (though starting at 0 is better for bar plots)
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.39, 1), oob = scales::squish) +
  
  # Custom Fill Color for Loss Functions (retained original labels/colors)
  scale_fill_manual(labels = expression(italic(L[membrane]), italic(L[spike])), 
                    values=c("#FC4E07", "#00AFBB"),
                    name = "Loss Function:") +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top", 
        legend.title = element_text(size=13, face="bold"), 
        legend.key.size = unit(0.7, 'cm'),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

                                            'Low focus'))

                    name = "Indicator Type:") +

  theme(legend.position = "top", 
        legend.title = element_text(size=10, face = "bold"), 
        axis.text.x = element_text( hjust = 1),

Figure: Feature analysis based on boxplot


integ = read.csv("integrate_20.csv", T)
{
  integ$class1 = ''
  integ[which(integ$label == "Intimacy" |integ$label == "non_Intimacy" ),'class1'] = 'Intimacy-related group'
  integ[which(integ$label == "Empathy" |integ$label == "non_Empathy" ),'class1'] = 'Empathy-related group'
  integ[which(integ$label == "Competition" |integ$label == "Cooperation" ),'class1'] = 'Competition-related group'
  integ[which(integ$label == "Low Focus" |integ$label == "High Focus" ),'class1'] = 'Focus-related group'
  
  vars = c('sPD_M', 'sPD_SD', 'sPD_H_PD', 'sPAS_M', 'sPAS_SD', 'sPD_M_diff', 'sPD_H_PD_diff', 'sPD_CS', 'sPAS_M_diff', 'sPAS_CS')
  for(var in vars){
    integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), var] = (integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), var]-min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), var]))/(max(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), var]) - min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), var]))         
    integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), var] = (integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), var]-min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), var]))/(max(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), var]) - min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), var]))         
    integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), var] = (integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), var]-min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), var]))/(max(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), var]) - min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), var]))         
    integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), var] = (integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), var]-min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), var]))/(max(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), var]) - min(integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), var]))         
    } 
  
  names(integ)[3] = 'sPD_H_PS'
  vars[3]= 'sPD_H_PS'
  names(integ)[9] = 'sPD_H_PS_diff'
  vars[7]= 'sPD_H_PS_diff'
}

Figure: Feature analysis based on KNN-2D distribution map



sample = integ[which(integ$class1 == "Intimacy-related group"), c('sPD_M_diff', 'sPD_CS', 'label')]
sample = integ[which(integ$class1 == "Empathy-related group"), c('sPD_M_diff', 'sPD_CS', 'label')]
sample = integ[which(integ$class1 == "Competition-related group"), c('sPD_M_diff', 'sPD_CS', 'label')]
sample = integ[which(integ$class1 == "Focus-related group"), c('sPD_M_diff', 'sPD_CS', 'label')]

# (Visualization 5) 2D distibution plot
{
  names(sample)[1:2] = c('V1','V2')
  sample$label = as.numeric(factor(sample$label))
  gridSize <- 150
  v1limits <- c(min(sample[,1]),max(sample[,1]))
  tmpV1 <- seq(v1limits[1],v1limits[2],len=gridSize)
  v2limits <- c(min(sample[,2]),max(sample[,2]))
  tmpV2 <- seq(v2limits[1],v2limits[2],len=gridSize)
  
  xgrid <- expand.grid(tmpV1,tmpV2)
  names(xgrid) <- names(sample[,1:2])
  knn1grid <- class::knn(train=sample[,1:2], test=xgrid, cl=sample[,3], k=50)
  V3 <- as.numeric(as.vector(knn1grid))
  xgrid <- cbind(xgrid, V3)
  
  point_shapes <- c(15,17)
  point_colours <- c("#005D8F", "#F2A202", "#7570B3")  # c("#005D8F", "#F2A202")
  point_size = 1
  ytrain = sample[,3]
  xtrain = sample[,1:2]
  ggplot(xgrid, aes(V1,V2)) +
    geom_point(col=point_colours[knn1grid], shape=16, size=0.3) +
    geom_point(data=xtrain, aes(V1,V2), col=point_colours[ytrain],
               shape=point_shapes[ytrain], size=point_size, show.legend = TRUE) +
    geom_contour(data=xgrid, aes(x=V1, y=V2, z=V3), breaks=2, col="grey30") +
    ggtitle('Intimacy and non-Intimacy') +
    # ggtitle('Empathy and non-Empathy') +
    # ggtitle('Competition and Cooperation') +
    # ggtitle('Low focus and High focus') +
